Draw a blinded, class-stratified sample of candidate pairs for review

Source: R/clerical.R
clerical_sample.Rd

Draw a blinded, class-stratified sample of candidate pairs for review

Usage

clerical_sample(
  per_candidate,
  n_per_class,
  seed,
  id = "id",
  candidate = "candidate",
  class = "evidence_class",
  cols = NULL
)

Arguments

per_candidate

data.frame of candidate pairs, e.g. the `per_candidate` element of [resolve_ordered_classes()].

n_per_class

rows to sample from each evidence class; a class with fewer rows contributes all of them.

seed

integer, REQUIRED. The draw must be reproducible to be auditable, and a default seed would smuggle a constant into every study's methods section; the seed belongs in yours. The global random state is saved and restored, so calling this does not perturb the caller's randomness.

id, candidate, class

column names.

cols

columns to show the reviewer. Defaults to everything except `class` – which is never shown, whatever `cols` says.

Value

list of two data.frames. `sheet`: `review_id`, the `cols`, and an empty `reviewer_verdict` column, shuffled – give this to the reviewer. `key`: `review_id`, `id`, `candidate`, `class` – keep this from the reviewer, then hand both to [clerical_precision()].
